> == 8a41d5202: vendor provenance, patch paths, Kind note ==
> - provenance.sh run live: all 6 crates ok (index = download = README, diff -r identical), exit 0. Tampering: one byte appended to vendor/managed/src/lib.rs gives 'managed 0.8.0: vendor/managed differs', exit 1. Good.
> - **P2: the script is fail-open when the README table can't be read.** I renamed the table header by one word ('License' to 'Licence'). The sed range then matches nothing, zero crates are checked, and it prints 'provenance: every vendored crate is the published one' with exit 0. Also, `[ -d vendor/$name ] || continue` skips a row silently, and a vendored directory missing from the table is never checked. The README-row test still passes in both cases. Fix: count the crates checked, and exit 1 unless the count equals the VENDORED list (6), or unless every vendor/<dir> in the patch table was checked. Fail too when the header isn't found.

> - The README and test docs now say integrity versus provenance, and the WIRE Kind note is right.
> 
> == 7ca3af285: netd's receive loop and the review-2 tests ==
> - receiver::receive: every exit resets through t, then calls report once. The IRQ fault ends the loop; only Fault::Timeout loops. The bin's report is the data-free BROKEN send. NetServer::sent acts only on BROKEN from the badge registered by expect_reports_on, which refuses badges below 2^63. Checkpoint 2's P2-1 is closed.
> - I planted 11 bugs and reverted each; **all 11 were caught**:
>   - rx descriptors not rewritten on re-offer (my earlier survivor): `a_scribbled_descriptor_is_rewritten_when_offered_again`;
>   - non-wrapping rx next_used, rx next_avail, tx next_used and tx next_avail (my earlier survivor, now four variants): `the_ring_counters_wrap`;
>   - receiver without the reset, without the report, and returning silently on an IRQ error: the IRQ-failure and lie tests;
>   - the panic hook without its STATUS write: `a_panic_resets_the_device`;
>   - `sent` ignoring the badge, and `expect_reports_on` accepting a low badge: `only_the_receive_threads_report_breaks_the_device`.
> - netd tests: 17 + 1 + 8 passed.
> 
> == ddb5c4732: the P1 and the P3s ==
> - **P1 closed.** with_overrides now counts sum of max(o.in_flight, default) + (buckets - #overrides) x default. That is the true worst case: each override slot is either the override's bucket or a default one that took its place. `fits` does the same per resource, which may over-count across resources, and that is safe. The regression test `the_worst_order_never_passes_the_headroom` fills badges in the worst order and refuses sshd 24 with steward 2.
> - Milestone check: sshd 23 + max(2, 5) + 4 x 5 = 48 <= 64 - 16, exactly at the bound. sshd's 23 = one waiting accept + 2 x 11 sessions, consistent with NAMESPACES.
> - **Hook.** run_panic_hook is pub(crate) on the machine and pub only on the host, for tests. A later panicker spins, bounded at 2^24, on HOOK_DONE; a panic inside the hook waits out the bound and then exits. The race test holds a slow hook and asserts the second panicker hasn't finished.
> - **netd arming.** A flag swap, then len, then base (Release). The hook reads base, then len (Acquire), so it never pairs one mapping's base with another's length. The test re-arms with a second mapping, which is refused, and still resets the first.
> - New tests: the labelled Twrite is refused at open and after (equal labels then wait), and `parked_write.rs` parks, abandons and expires a waiting write through serve_parking.
> - **rt fuzz extended.** A Tree write at an odd offset waits, and the op mix includes mint_rooted/unmint and with_overrides. Spot run of ninep_server with the corpus carried over: 412,840 runs in 121 s, 2,843 new units, peak RSS 531 MB, no crash, exit 0.
> 
> == ab45ef0c6: parked.rs ==
> LONGEST is now 2 s, and B stops when A's thread has finished, asserting it woke A. If A expires under load, the test now fails with a message instead of hanging. That closes the race I described. parked and parked_write, run three times with --test-threads=8: all pass (3 + 1 each run).
> 
> == Regression sweep ==
> cargo test for redoubt-rt, netd, consoled, blkd, bootfsd and keyd: every suite passes, none failed.
> 
> Scope: tools/vendor-check, vendor/README, docs (WIRE, NAMESPACES), libs/rt, servers/netd. Additive, with no change to kernel/, model/ or K5 paths.
